arxiv-1708-06452.title: Studies on the Pea Pattern Sequence
arxiv-1708-06452.creator: André Pedroso Kowacs
arxiv-1708-06452.description: Abstract 1. Abstract In this paper we formally define the family of sequences known as “Pea Pattern sequences”. We then analyze its behaviour and conditions for fixed points. The paper ends with a list of fixed points from base 2 to 10 . 2.

arxiv-2103-00487.title: Network Growth From Global and Local Influential Nodes
arxiv-2103-00487.creator: Jiaojiao Jiang, and Sanjay Jha
arxiv-2103-00487.description: Abstract In graph theory and network analysis, node degree is defined as a simple but powerful centrality to measure the local influence of node in a complex network. Preferential attachment based on node degree has been widely adopted for modeling network growth. However, many evidences exist which show deviation of real network growth from what a pure degree-based model suggests.

arxiv-2107-03734.title: Turbulent kinetic energy dissipation from colliding ice floes
arxiv-2107-03734.creator: Trygve K. Løken, Aleksey Marchenko, Thea J. Ellevold, Jean Rabault, Atle Jensen
arxiv-2107-03734.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Trygve K. Løken, Aleksey Marchenko, Thea J. Ellevold, Jean Rabault, Atle Jensen. Increased knowledge about wave attenuation processes in sea ice, and hence atmosphere-wave-ice-ocean energy transfer, is necessary to improve sea ice dynamics models used for climate modeling and offshore applications. The aim of this study is to generate such much needed data by investigating colliding ice floes dynamics in a large-scale experiment and directly measuring and quantifying the turbulent kinetic energy (TKE).

arxiv-2111-09001.title: A study of Intrinsic γ \gamma -ray Emission for Fermi /LAT-detected BL Lacs
arxiv-2111-09001.creator: X. H. Ye, X. T. Zeng, W. X. Yang, H. S. Huang, Y. H. Xuan, J. W. Huang, Z. Zhang, Z. Y. Pei, J. H. Yang, J. H. Fan
arxiv-2111-09001.description: Abstract BL Lacs are one subclass of blazars with highly energetic γ \gamma -ray emission, which is strongly boosted by a relativistic beaming effect. The latest catalogue of the 10 years of Fermi /LAT data ( Abdollahi et al. 2020 ) and the γ \gamma -ray Doppler factors in Pei et al.

arxiv-2306-00718.title: A Strong Sustainability Paradigm Based Analytical Hierarchy Process (SSP-AHP) Method to Evaluate Sustainable Healthcare Systems Journal: Ecological Indicators
arxiv-2306-00718.creator: Jarosław Wątróbski, Aleksandra Bączkiewicz, Iga Rudawska
arxiv-2306-00718.description: Abstract The recent studies signify the growing concern of researchers towards monitoring and measuring sustainability performance at various levels and in many fields, including healthcare. However, there is no agreed approach to assessing the sustainability of health systems. Moreover, social indicators are less developed and less succinct.

arxiv-2307-09451.title: The effect of pressure-anisotropy-driven kinetic instabilities on magnetic field amplification in galaxy clusters
arxiv-2307-09451.creator: Y. Rappaz, J. Schober
arxiv-2307-09451.description: Abstract Context. The intracluster medium (ICM) is the low-density diffuse gas that fills the space between galaxies within galaxy clusters. It is primarily composed of magnetized plasma, which reaches virial temperatures of up to 10 8 ​ K 10^{8}\penalty\ \mathrm{K} , probably due to mergers of subhalos.

arxiv-2309-04551.title: Recursive Error Reduction for Regular Branching Programs
arxiv-2309-04551.creator: Eshan Chattopadhyay, Jyun-Jie Liao
arxiv-2309-04551.description: Abstract In a recent work, Chen, Hoza, Lyu, Tal and Wu (FOCS 2023) showed an improved error reduction framework for the derandomization of regular read-once branching programs (ROBPs). Their result is based on a clever modification to the inverse Laplacian perspective of space-bounded derandomization, which was originally introduced by Ahmadinejad, Kelner, Murtagh, Peebles, Sidford and Vadhan (FOCS 2020).

arxiv-2412-12803.title: Rare events statistics for ℤ d \mathbb{Z}^{d} map lattices coupled by collision Thanks: The research of W. Bahsoun was supported by EPSRC grant EP/V053493/1. The work of M. Phalempin was partially supported by ARC Laureat Fellowship FL230100088 and by FABuLOuS project within “Bando Ricercatori a Fir
arxiv-2412-12803.creator: Wael Bahsoun, Maxence Phalempin
arxiv-2412-12803.description: Abstract . Understanding the statistics of collisions among locally confined gas particles poses a major challenge. In this work we investigate ℤ d \mathbb{Z}^{d} -map lattices coupled by collision with simplified local dynamics that offer significant insights for the above challenging problem.

arxiv-2510-17582.title: Non-interference analysis of bounded labeled Petri nets
arxiv-2510-17582.creator: Ning Ran, Zhengguang Wu, Shaokang Zhang, Zhou He, Carla Seatzu
arxiv-2510-17582.description: Abstract This paper focuses on a fundamental problem on information security of bounded labeled Petri nets: non-interference analysis. As in hierarchical control, we assume that a system is observed by users at different levels, namely high-level users and low-level users. The output events produced by the firing of transitions are also partitioned into high-level output events and low-level output events.

britannica-1911-thayer-james-bradley.title: Thayer, James Bradley (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-thayer-james-bradley.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-thayer-james-bradley.description: Article 'Thayer, James Bradley' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 26), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. writer and educationist, was born at Haverhill, Massachusetts, on the 15th of January 1831. He graduated at Harvard College in 1852, and at the Harvard Law School in 1856, in which year he was admitted to the bar of Suffolk county and began to practise in Boston.

pmc-10926554.title: Population divergence in nutrient-temperature interactions in Pieris rapae
pmc-10926554.creator: Anna L. Parker, Joel G. Kingsolver
pmc-10926554.description: The interaction between larval host plant quality and temperature can influence the short-term physiological rates and life-history traits of insect herbivores. These factors can vary locally, resulting in local adaptation in responses to diet and temperature, but the comparison of these interactions between populations is infrequently carried out.

pmc-11349727.title: Notch transcriptional target tmtc1 maintains vascular homeostasis
pmc-11349727.creator: Na Yoon Paik, Jacob Neethling, Mumtaz Anwar, Prerak Gupta, Mark A Sanborn, Zekun Shen, Thilinie Bandara, James Hyun, L A Naiche, Jan K Kitajewski, Jalees Rehman, Jae-Won Shin, Dolly Mehta, Kostandin V Pajcini
pmc-11349727.description: Proper lung function requires the maintenance of a tight endothelial barrier while simultaneously permitting the exchange of macromolecules and fluids to underlying tissue. Disruption of this barrier results in an increased vascular permeability in the lungs, leading to acute lung injury. In this study, we set out to determine whether transcriptional targets of Notch signaling function to preserve vascular integrity.

pmc-11492919.title: Daily Antiplatelets Other Than Aspirin Reduce Liver Cancer Risk but Increase Intracranial Hemorrhage Risk in Cirrhotic Patients
pmc-11492919.creator: Chern-Horng Lee, Cheng-Li Lin, Tzung-Hai Yen, Sen-Yung Hsieh
pmc-11492919.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeAspirin, known to reduce the risk of liver cancer, has been proposed as a preventive measure for patients with chronic hepatitis and cirrhosis. However, concerns regarding aspirin’s potential to cause gastrointestinal (GI) mucosal injury and bleeding have emerged. Several antiplatelets other than aspirin (APOA) that pose a smaller risk of GI bleeding than aspirin have been proposed as potential aspirin substitutes. This study investigated whether APOAs were effective at reducing the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).

pmc-13423508.title: Orientation Engineering in Flexible Ag2Se‐Based Thermoelectric Films
pmc-13423508.creator: Hao Wu, Xiao‐Lei Shi, Qingfeng Liu, Zhi‐Gang Chen
pmc-13423508.description: Flexible thermoelectrics convert body heat into electricity, offering a promising route towards self‐powered wearable electronics while overcoming the limitations of conventional batteries. Among emerging flexible thermoelectric materials, silver selenide (Ag2Se) has attracted widespread attention because it combines outstanding near‐room‐temperature thermoelectric performance with low cost, excellent mechanical flexibility, and superior biocompatibility.

pmc-13632108.title: Estimation of substitution and indel rates via k-mer statistics
pmc-13632108.creator: Mahmudur Rahman Hera, Paul Medvedev, David Koslicki, Antonio Blanca
pmc-13632108.description: Methods utilizing kk-mers are widely used in bioinformatics, yet our understanding of their statistical properties under realistic mutation models remains incomplete. Previously, substitution-only mutation models have been considered to derive precise expectations and variances for mutated kk-mers and intervals of mutated and non-mutated sequences.

pmc-13637262.title: Detection of thyroglobulin, TSH receptor and sodium-iodine symporter mRNA for identification of lymph node metastases in patients with papillary thyroid carcer
pmc-13637262.creator: Lei Gao, Yu Bao, Tie-Xin Li, Guo-Qing Liu, Fu-Xing Zhang, Ying-Chao Chen, Bing Han, Lu Li, Huai-Dong Song, Mu-Lin Liu, Mei Dong
pmc-13637262.description: BackgroundPapillary thyroid carcer (PTC) is the most prevalent endocrine malignancy, with the morbidity increase in recent years. The presence of metastatic lymph nodes stands as a significant predictor for recurrent occurrences of the disease. In this study, we explored the utility of biomarkers in aiding the identification of lymph node metastases in patients with PTC.

pmc-13647597.title: The association between multimorbidity in families and children’s healthcare use: a cross-sectional study of households in the Lolland Falster Health Study (LOFUS)
pmc-13647597.creator: Louise Bidstrup Jørgensen, Elisabeth Søndergaard, Volkert Siersma, Dagny Ros Nicolaisdottir, Randi Jepsen, Anne Møller
pmc-13647597.description: BackgroundChronic illness among adults is common, and an increasing number of children grow up in households where one or more adults live with long-term health conditions. While previous research has shown that parental physical or mental illness may influence children’s mental health, less is known about how adult multimorbidity affects children’s physical health and their healthcare use.
